content: The Cochrane Review, originally published in 2003 and updated in 2010, evaluated the use of a single intraoperative dose of dexamethasone to reduce post-tonsillectomy morbidity in children. Tonsillectomy remains a common surgical procedure globally, but postoperative complications, such as pain, nausea, and vomiting, continue to pose significant clinical challenges despite advancements in surgical and anesthetic techniques. The review included 19 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials involving 1,756 pediatric participants under the age of 18 who underwent tonsillectomy or adenotonsillectomy. The studies assessed the effects of a single intravenous dose of dexamethasone (ranging from 0.15 to 1.0 mg/kg) administered during surgery. Data were extracted and analyzed using a random-effects model to ensure robust statistical evaluation. The findings demonstrated that children who received dexamethasone were approximately 50% less likely to experience vomiting within the first 24 hours post-surgery compared to those who received a placebo (risk ratio [RR] 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.41 to 0.58; P < 0.00001). This translates to a number needed to treat (NNT) of five, meaning that for every five children treated with dexamethasone, one case of postoperative vomiting would be prevented. Additionally, children in the dexamethasone group were more likely to progress to a soft or solid diet by the first postoperative day compared to the placebo group (RR 1.45; 95% CI 1.15 to 1.83; P = 0.001). Pain levels, as measured by a visual analog scale (VAS) ranging from 0 to 10, were also significantly reduced in the dexamethasone group. The mean difference in pain scores was -1.07 (95% CI -1.73 to -0.41; P = 0.001), indicating a clinically meaningful reduction in pain from an average score of 4.72 to 3.65. Importantly, no adverse events related to dexamethasone administration were reported in the included studies. The authors concluded that a single intraoperative dose of dexamethasone is a safe, effective, and cost-efficient intervention for reducing postoperative morbidity in children undergoing tonsillectomy.
